classification.difficultyReason: Apply combinations to select players, head positions and triangle vertices; recognise that any three circle points form a triangle. The committee requires multiplying two independent selections, directly modelled in the supplied example.

children.label: a
children.prompt: 10 people meet to play doubles tennis. How many ways can 4 people be selected to play the first game (ignore subsequent arrangement into pairs)?

answer.worked:
Select 4 people from 10; their order does not matter.
$$\begin{aligned}{}^{10}C_{4}&=\frac{10!}{4!6!}\\&=210\end{aligned}$$
There are 210 ways.

children.label: b
children.prompt: A coin is tossed 5 times. How many ways are there of getting 2 heads?

answer.worked:
Choose which 2 of the 5 tosses are heads. The other 3 tosses are tails.
$$\begin{aligned}{}^{5}C_{2}&=\frac{5!}{2!3!}\\&=10\end{aligned}$$
There are 10 ways.

children.label: c
children.prompt: A workplace has 4 women and 6 men. How many ways can you select 2 women and 2 men to form a committee?

answer.worked:
Choose 2 of the 4 women and 2 of the 6 men. Multiply the numbers of choices.
$$\begin{aligned}{}^{4}C_{2}\times{}^{6}C_{2}&=6\times15\\&=90\end{aligned}$$
There are 90 ways.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Ten points are arranged equally around a circle. How many ways are there of drawing a triangle using these points?

spec.description: Unshaded circle with ten equally spaced filled points. Indexed labels run clockwise from A_1 at the top to A_6 at the bottom and A_10 at the upper left. Labels remain outside the circle at native 10 pt.
spec.mathematics: Ten distinct concyclic points; no chords or triangle are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All circle geometry and point labels are permanent question givens.

answer.worked:
Any 3 of the points form one triangle, and their order does not matter.
$$\begin{aligned}{}^{10}C_{3}&=\frac{10!}{3!7!}\\&=120\end{aligned}$$
There are 120 triangles.
